                    ### Question
                    A 61-year-old man sustains an intracranial injury to a nerve that also passes through the parotid gland. Which of the following is a possible consequence of this injury?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Loss of taste from posterior 1/3 of tongue
opb. Loss of general sensation in anterior 2/3 of tongue
opc. Paralysis of lateral rectus muscle
opd. Changes in hearing
ope. Horner's syndrome

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Injury to a nerve passing through the parotid gland can affect the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), leading to loss of taste from the posterior 1/3 of the tongue. This is supported by the fact that the glossopharyngeal nerve is involved in taste sensation. The evidence paths mentioning the glossopharyngeal nerve structure and its association with taste loss further support this outcome.
